governanceNotes: D1 batch 64 (2026-09-26): identity deferred (UMBRELLA-SCOPE / IDENTITY-DUPLICATION with the neurocognitive cluster). The identity is the Mental Disorders catalog umbrella for acquired neurocognitive decline (38 CFR 4.130 framework), and the located evidence supports no outgoing catalog edge: (i) all candidate secondary outcomes - depressive-disorder, anxiety-disorder, insomnia, urinary-incontinence - are already carried by published sibling windows (dementia, cognitive-disorder, alzheimer-s-disease, memory-loss), so authoring from this umbrella would double-claim the same clinical territory (identity-duplication guard; no evidence recycled from those windows per ME-29); (ii) the located prospective outcomes literature for cognitive impairment (falls and disability via cognitive frailty, delirium risk, progression to dementia) is indexed to frailty constructs, to acute hospitalization, or to specific dementias - not to this umbrella as the index condition - so the umbrella has no identity-specific quantification of any catalog-fit outcome; (iii) progression from mild to major neurocognitive disorder is within-umbrella and cannot be authored as a secondary-condition edge. Reopening conditions: (a) a cohort using this umbrella (rather than a specific dementia) as the index exposure with a catalog-fit secondary outcome quantified and confounding (vascular disease, depression, sensory impairment) adjusted; or (b) a governance decision treating this identity as a rating-schedule classification header rather than a mapping source, consistent with its no-diagnosis-specific-code catalog note.
